To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) excited Auger decay processes in clusters can lead to the formation of trications and (ii) the decay mechanism is based on an ultrafast Coulombic energy transfer process from an excited dicationic mononuclear species to a neighboring neutral monomer.
(i) the decay of a core-hole dication in a cluster can lead to the formation of tricationic clusters and (ii) the decay is ultrafast.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the fundamental processes that govern the interaction of matter with electromagnetic radiation.
the study of the electronic and structural properties of clusters and their response to external perturbations.
the electronic properties of small clusters and their response to external fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Auger decay of a 1 s core hole in a dimer of neon is a two-step process, involving the initial formation of the dicationic monomeric state, followed by a rapid energy-transfer process, leading to the tricationic dimer.
the Auger decay of the Ne2 2p−1 state is a very fast process, which occurs on the femtosecond time scale and leads to the formation of the Ne2+3 state.

the present work provides a clear and compelling demonstration of the importance of Coulombic energy transfer for Auger decay in clusters, and the possibility of triple ionization by Auger decay in a cluster.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Auger effect is a universal phenomenon in clusters and that the Auger decay channels can be modified and even new channels opened by cluster formation.
it shows that the Auger decay of a core hole in a cluster can be much faster than the Auger decay in the isolated monomers.
we have shown that the Auger decay of the Ne 1s hole in Ne2 is ultrafast and leads to the formation of Ne3+2+.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Auger decay of a core-excited dicationic cluster can be very different from the decay of a core excited dimer.
the Auger decay of a core hole in a cluster can be very different from that in an isolated atom or molecule.
the decay of a dicationic monomeric species can be very different in a cluster.
